inputs.receptor_source: Notebook 2 output, verified by SHA256 match

box.derivation: centroid of crystallographic 1JI in 5SB1 chain A

usage: PLIP [-h] (-f INPUT [INPUT ...] | -i PDBID [PDBID ...]) [-o OUTPATH |
            -O] [--rawstring] [-v] [-q] [-s] [-p] [-x] [-t] [-z]
            [--name OUTPUTFILENAME] [-y] [--maxthreads MAXTHREADS]
            [--breakcomposite] [--altlocation] [--nofix] [--nofixfile]
            [--nopdbcanmap] [--dnareceptor]

plip_version_note: Not all PLIP builds support --version. When the short flag fails, the --help output is stored as the fallback. 'plip_available' is a Boolean availability flag, not a version.

protocol.box_center_source: derived in Notebook 2 from the 1JI centroid
protocol.rmsd_method: Direct heavy-atom RMSD between poses in the receptor frame. No superposition is performed; translation and rotation are part of the pose. RMSD is symmetry-corrected by minimizing over graph-valid heavy-atom automorphisms of the reference ligand. Atom correspondence is derived from Meeko SMILES IDX metadata and a stereochemistry-aware full-graph mapping. Unresolved mappings receive no numeric RMSD.
protocol.representative_pose_rule: Most central of the three seed poses, defined as the pose with the lowest mean pairwise direct RMSD to the other two.
protocol.plip_input_pose: The representative seed's pose, not necessarily the best-scoring pose. Rows where the two differ by >= 1 kcal/mol are listed under 'representative_vs_best_disagreements'.

priority_rule.calibration_note: Thresholds are user-set. 'calibrated' is true only when the control-docking ROC 95% CI lower bound is >= 0.6 and the control run was full scope (20 actives, 200 decoys, 3 seeds). Even then, the specific cut-offs are not empirically optimised.

control_docking.scope_note: Full scope is 20 actives, 200 property-matched decoys, 3 Vina seeds per compound. This run used 20 actives, 20 decoys, 1 seed(s). AUC confidence intervals are correspondingly wider and enrichment estimates noisier.
control_docking.note: Controls confirm that the protocol can discriminate DDR1 actives from property-matched decoys. They do NOT validate the absolute tier thresholds.

caveats: Vina scores are not Delta-G values.
PLIP contacts are geometric predictions, not measured affinities.
Only one receptor structure (5SB1) was used; DFG-state and receptor flexibility were not explored.
Ligands were docked in their neutral form. pH 7.4 protonation states were not enumerated. Amines, amidines, and carboxylic acids are particularly sensitive to protonation state.

Pose RMSD is symmetry-corrected using graph automorphisms and calculated directly in the receptor coordinate frame without superposition. Atom-order and atom-type checks must pass; unresolved mappings are not assigned a numeric RMSD. Review any UNRESOLVED candidate before interpreting its tier.

Tier thresholds (-10 and -8 kcal/mol) are user-set and were NOT calibrated against DDR1 actives or decoys: the control-docking ROC was run in reduced scope. Re-run the controls at full scope (CONTROL_SEEDS = SEEDS, CONTROL_N_DECOYS = 200) before publishing any claim that the tiers rank known DDR1 binders above property-matched decoys.
Priority_tier is a two-factor gate based on pose stability and best Vina score. Interaction counts and pose reproducibility are reported as context and are NOT part of the tier decision.
Overall_QC reflects whether the pipeline ran cleanly, not whether the pose is biologically trustworthy. Interpret it together with Pose_consistency and Priority_tier.
